reason: planning stopped before any code was written: the critic judged that the reading misread the request: The request says a conflict "blocks dispatch until the prompt and the rule agree", and its acceptance line says agent-instruction changes are currently not checked. The reading contradicts itself on this. Its first assumption says the check "runs at reading/plan admission when the request edits a prompt file". Its second lets the function stay unwired ("else the function is exposed"). It also narrows "an agent prompt" to the verifier prompt only. The plan follows the unwired branch, so as planned no real prompt edit is ever blocked. That is the very state the request asks to change. (round 1 of 5). I checked the plan's references against the snapshot and they are accurate: `judge` at verify.rs:408, the D43 finding at :601, `request_reading_mismatch` at :626, the test module at :1140, `VERIFIER_FRAME` public at athena-context lib.rs:50, and the three verifier.md files. The table-plus-pure-function shape fits the Files line and one producer run, and the dependents list matches what grep finds for the module's callers. There are three problems. First, the plan calls the check unwired and its CHANGELOG entry says it is not in any gate, so the requested blocking behavior is never shown. Yet the plan's own shipped-prompt test already runs in `cargo test` on every candidate, so a producer edit to verifier.md that contradicts a rule would fail Athena's checks. The plan should claim that as the enforcement point and demonstrate it. Second, the required-field check accepts any whole-word match. `commands`, `criterion` and `verdict` are ordinary prose words, and `commands` appears several times in verifier.md outside the instruction that names the field. Deleting "list them in commands exactly as run" would therefore still pass, and the criterion-3 test hides this by deleting every occurrence. Third, the three-word negation lookback has an obvious hole: "Never refuse; accept uncited commands" passes. The module-docs drift guard is also circular, because it reads verify.rs, which contains the table itself. Findings: major: The plan never shows the requested outcome: a prompt edit that conflicts with a rule is blocked. The plan presents the check as unwired, even though its own test already acts as a gate. (Plan Decision 1, step 4 (CHANGELOG), criterion 4 demonstration); major: A field counts as present if its name appears anywhere as a whole word. For the common words commands, criterion and verdict, ordinary prose satisfies the check, so dropping the field instruction goes undetected. (Decision 3, step 2 (field presence), criterion 3 demonstration); major: The three-word negation lookback has an obvious false negative: a negation word aimed at a different verb suppresses a real contradiction. (Decision 2, step 2 (`phrase_conflicts` negation lookback)); minor: The drift guard reads verify.rs, which contains the table itself. Unless the test restricts itself to the `//!` header lines, it always passes. (Decision 4(b), `table_ids_appear_in_the_module_docs`); minor: The demonstration contradicts itself on its threshold and measures the wrong quantity for the criterion. (Criterion 5 demonstration); minor: Changing CHANGELOG.md breaks criterion 7 as worded, and reading.rs is an expected deliverable the plan leaves untouched. The verifier may flag either one.
